title: An ultra performance liquid chromatography coupled with high resolution mass spectrometry method for the screening of cianotoxins content in drinking water samples
author: di pofi, Favero, et al.

steps.title: Prepare internal standard solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve cyanotoxin standards to obtain a solution containing 0.1 µg/L of each analyte and 1 µg/L Nodularin (internal standard) in a solvent mixture of 70 % water : 30 % acetonitrile containing 10 mM formic acid; do not perform any extraction on this solution.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Spike four aliquots of water with the internal‑standard solution to achieve final concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 µg/L for each cyanotoxin; these will be used to construct the calibration curve.

steps.title: Collect and pre‑treat water sample
steps.instruction: Take 250 mL of drinking‑water sample, freeze it, filter the thawed sample, then spike with Nodularin to a final concentration of 1 µg/L before extraction.

steps.title: Extract cyanotoxins by SPE
steps.instruction: Pass the spiked, filtered sample through a Carbograph 4 solid‑phase extraction cartridge under the conditions described in the updated method; elute the retained toxins for subsequent LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Configure UPLC system and gradient
steps.instruction: Install an Acquity UPLC BEH C18 column (2.1 mm ID × 100 mm, 1.7 µm). Prepare mobile phase A as water + 10 mM formic acid and mobile phase B as acetonitrile + 10 mM formic acid. Set the column temperature to 45 °C and the flow rate to 0.5 µL/min. Apply the gradient exactly as listed in Table 1: 0 → 4 min %As 40 % %Af 45 %; 0 → 7 min %As 90 % %Af 70 %; 0 → 8 min %As 40 % %Af 50 %; 0 → 9 min %As 30 % %Af 10 %; 0 → 12 min %As 40 % %Af 50 %; 0 → 13 min %As 90 % %Af 90 %; total run 16 min (gradient data reproduced verbatim: "0 → 4 40 45 0 90 → 70 4 → 8 30 → 10 40 30 → 0 10 → 12 40 50 → 0 12 → 13 40 50 → 90 13 → 16 40 90 → 90").

steps.title: Set mass spectrometer parameters
steps.instruction: Operate the XEVO G2‑S Q‑TOF in sensitivity mode with positive ionisation. Use a scan time of 0.5 s, source temperature 130 °C, desolvation temperature 500 °C, and desolvation gas flow of 1000.0 L/h. Enable lock‑mass correction throughout the run.

steps.title: Acquire full‑scan and MS/MS data
steps.instruction: Collect a full‑scan mass spectrum from m/z 50–1200 and acquire targeted MS/MS spectra for each toxin using the collision energy (CE) and fragment m/z values listed in Table 2; ensure that the molecular ion and its specific fragment are observed at the retention time given for each toxin.

steps.title: Process data and confirm toxin identity
steps.instruction: Identify each cyanotoxin only when its molecular ion and the corresponding fragment ion appear at the same retention time (as listed in Table 2). Quantify using the calibration curve prepared in Step 2. Report limits of detection (0.002–0.047 µg/L) and calculate limits of quantitation as three times the LOD. The total chromatographic run time is 16 minutes.
